Your transition into  your personal anecdote about teaching resonated. I was never formally a teacher nor even a tutor, as formal titles. However, I often found myself in a role of instructor, tutor, exam preparation facilitator, team lead, etc. There was an expectation of expertise. At a minimum, there was an expectation of knowing how to obtain the correct answers and information when needed. Needing to know and understand a subject well enough to also explain it to someone else helped me to deliberately focus my personal learning in a way that was accidentally, "Active Learning," or, "Active Recall." I pictured a wall in front of the person or team that I was helping. It didn't matter if I could easily comprehend a subject. What mattered was getting that person past the wall that was keeping *THEM* from understanding the subject. Everything that I was learning also needed two or three different ways to better explain it to someone else that wasn't immediately understanding it.
